primary.title: The Jamaica Letter
primary.author: Simón Bolívar
primary.rationale: A foundational document outlining Bolívar's vision for the future of Spanish America and his critique of Spanish rule. Widely translated and studied.

primary.title: Cartagena Manifesto
primary.author: Simón Bolívar
primary.rationale: An early important political document where Bolívar analyzes the causes of the failure of the Second Republic of Venezuela and outlines his political thought.

primary.title: Discourse of Angostura
primary.author: Simón Bolívar
primary.rationale: A pivotal speech delivered to the Congress of Angostura, presenting Bolívar's political philosophy and proposals for the governance of Gran Colombia.

secondary.title: Simón Bolívar: A Life
secondary.author: Marie Arana
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded biography of Bolívar, offering a modern scholarly perspective on his life and impact.

secondary.title: Bolívar: American Liberator
secondary.author: Salvador de Madariaga
secondary.rationale: Although published before 1976, this is a classic and highly influential scholarly biography that remains a cornerstone for Bolívar studies. Its enduring relevance justifies its inclusion.

secondary.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. III: Integrated Empires and Revolutions, 1780-1850
secondary.author: Leslie Bethell (Editor)
secondary.rationale: This volume contains scholarly chapters by leading historians that contextualize Bolívar's actions within the broader independence movements of Latin America.

suggestions.notes: The primary sources are foundational texts by Bolívar. Secondary sources include a recent comprehensive biography and a classic scholarly work, as well as a chapter from a major academic history of Latin America.
